title: Composition-dependent structural, thermal and electrical properties of LiCl–Li 2 O–P 2 O 5  phosphate glasses
content: Lithium-containing phosphate glasses have attracted considerable attention as potential solid electrolyte materials because of their compositional flexibility and their ability to support ion transport. Based on this idea, researchers prepared a series of phosphate glasses from the ternary system x(LiCl–Li2O)/(1 − x) P2O5. They used x values of 25, 29, 33.33, 38, 43, and 48%. The glass densities were measured using Archimedes' method. The team conducted thermal and structural characterizations using DSC, infrared spectroscopy, and Raman spectroscopy. They also investigated electrical conductivity and dielectric relaxation using impedance spectroscopy across a frequency range of 10 Hz to 1 MHz at various temperatures. The density values depend strongly on composition. Both density and molar volume change consistently with the modifier concentration. The glass transition and crystallization temperatures exhibit non-monotonic variations with increasing LiCl/Li2O content, reflecting the composition-dependent thermal behaviour of the investigated glasses. Spectroscopic results indicate progressive depolymerization of the phosphate network due to structural changes caused by the modifier. These findings provide insights into the influence of LiCl/Li2O content on the structural and electrical properties of phosphate glasses, highlighting their potential for further investigation as solid electrolyte candidates.
